title: Causal invariant dimension-preserving network rules give Einstein equations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Causal invariant dimension-preserving network rules give Einstein equations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Network replacement rules that are causal invariant and maintain a fixed number of dimensions will almost inevitably produce large-scale behavior close to the vacuum Einstein equations of general relativity, analogous to how Navier–Stokes behavior emerges from cellular automaton fluids.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But I suspect that if one has replacement rules that are causal invariant and that in effect successfully maintain a fixed number of dimensions they will almost inevitably lead to behavior that follows something close to the Einstein equations.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “The Phenomenon of Gravity” (from p. 530), p. 535. Scope: causal invariant network rewriting systems and general relativity

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-25: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.51

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Specific rules can be checked now and counterexamples may settle an overly broad implication. Existing public rule sets are too selected and too small to determine prevalence over the full claimed class.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define an ensemble of causal-invariant, dimension-preserving rewrite rules, derive their coarse-grained curvature dynamics, and compare them with vacuum Einstein solutions. Frequent convergence would support 'almost inevitably'; valid counterexamples with non-Einstein large-scale behavior would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Large-scale simulations are computationally expensive.

'Almost inevitably' requires a measure over rules.

Dimension preservation and coarse-graining are not uniquely defined.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.52
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The vacuum Einstein condition and the causal-invariance and fixed-dimension hypotheses are mathematically meaningful, and special-case arguments plus the lattice-gas analogy to Navier–Stokes exist. They do not amount to a theorem that almost every such rule yields the Einstein equations. Gravitational-wave tests constrain the macroscopic equation, not the claim about network rules.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For network rewrite rules that are causally invariant and hold dimension fixed, test whether the large-scale curvature satisfies the vacuum Einstein condition that the Ricci tensor vanishes, against rules that conserve dimension but produce other curvature equations. A general proof or a quantified survey would confirm 'almost inevitably'; a positive-measure family of counterexample rules would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Vacuum Einstein behavior can emerge from more than one continuum limit, so a matching equation does not isolate the stated hypotheses.

'Almost inevitably' quantifies over an undefined class of rules.
